mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession (UNRATE < 3%).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and depresses equity prices, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or GDP growth rebounds above trend within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, pushing firms to raise wages and prices, which increases input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY) falls below 2% during the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in INDPRO (index below previous month for three consecutive months) signals weakening industrial production and lower corporate revenues, which causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or INDPRO rebounds above trend within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST over two months indicates falling housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of co-declining episodes, or either GDPC1 or HOUST rebounds within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 2% while CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 4% for three months signals a failed monetary easing, where inflation remains high despite rate cuts, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% AND CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% for three months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or inflation falls below 3% within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and UNRATE above 4% for two months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both > 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or UNRATE falls below 4% within the next month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in RSAFS above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings and reduced consumption, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or RSAFS falls below its moving average within the horizon.
